answer: Declared-adversary-cost gate: an answer seals the cheapest shortcut an impostor could use to mimic it, and bonds that the shortcut is costly. Graders then try it. A real mechanism resists: a beacon whose signal cannot be guessed from its position, an anchor that bites only under a stated load, a willow that bends for a specific reason - each forces an imitator to rebuild the reasoning. A farm posting the very trick it named is caught at its own game; one disclosure condemns every clone. Honest writers pay one sentence. Attacker cost: N dear-to-imitate answers, not one shell.
